enquiry: We produce a clear, colourless aqueous sucrose solution and want to monitor its sucrose concentration in-line. The solution flows through a 50 mm stainless steel pipe at 20 to 30 °C and normal pressure; the expected range is 5 to 15 % w/w and our quality limit is plus or minus 0.3 % w/w. Our laboratory refractometer is the reference method and stays in use. The analyser can stand in a dry, safe room 10 m from the pipe, and the line is cleaned in place with hot caustic once a day. A reading every minute is enough. Please propose a method and probe for a first trial.

items.finding: The text notes that temperature sensitivity of OH bands poses a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solutions in NIR and MIR, requiring tempered sample holders.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests that temperature compensation or control should be tested when measuring aqueous sucrose concentration to mitigate OH band sensitivity.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited text addresses general aqueous solutions in biopharmaceutical processing rather than sucrose specifically, so transfer to this exact system requires validation.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
